question: What is the purpose of the Perfect Attendance Program?
expected_answer: The Perfect Attendance Program recognizes employees' commitment, professionalism, quality performance, respect for Company time, and dedication through consistent and regular attendance. It also aims to encourage employee participation, regular attendance, productivity, and efficiency.
required_facets: Purpose, values recognized, attendance and productivity aims

question: What are the requirements for an employee to qualify for the Perfect Attendance Award?
expected_answer: An employee must have no absences except planned vacation leave with pay, no tardiness or undertime, no maternity leave, paternity leave, bereavement leave, honeymoon leave, emergency leave, or LWOP, and must have perfect attendance on all required overtime.
required_facets: Absence exception, tardiness/undertime, specified leave exclusions, required OT attendance

question: What period does HR use when checking attendance for the Perfect Attendance Award?
expected_answer: HR checks the employee's attendance from June of the year preceding the applicable year up to May of the applicable year.
required_facets: June of preceding year through May of applicable year

question: Can an employee still qualify for the Perfect Attendance Award if they take planned vacation leave with pay?
expected_answer: Yes. Planned vacation leave with pay is excluded from the absence restriction, based on the CompanyABC Work Schedule Policy. However, the employee must still satisfy all other Perfect Attendance criteria.
required_facets: Explicit Yes plus planned paid VL exception and other award requirements

question: What happens if an employee fails to log in or log out during the attendance period?
expected_answer: Failure to log in and log out shall automatically disqualify the employee from the Perfect Attendance Award.
required_facets: Automatic disqualification for failed in/out logs

question: What is the company's regular full-time work schedule?
expected_answer: The regular full-time work schedule is eight (8) hours per day, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., five (5) days per week from Monday to Friday, excluding holidays. Each working day includes an unpaid one-hour lunch break and two paid fifteen-minute breaks.
required_facets: 8h/day, 7:30–4:30, Mon–Fri, breaks and lunch treatment

question: How does the semi-flextime policy work for employees who arrive late in the morning?
expected_answer: The semi-flextime scheme allows employees to report from 7:30 a.m. and every 15 minutes thereafter until 9:00 a.m. without being considered tardy, but there is no grace period. The end of office hours is adjusted accordingly. For example, an employee who arrives at 8:29 a.m. has an official time-in of 8:30 a.m. and an adjusted time-out of 5:30 p.m.
required_facets: 15-minute increments, 7:30–9:00 window, no grace; 8:29 example

question: What are the regular break schedules during the workday?
expected_answer: The regular breaks are: Morning Break from 10:00–10:15 a.m., Lunch Break from 11:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m., Afternoon Break from 3:00–3:15 p.m., Dinner Break from 7:00–7:45 p.m., and Late Evening Break from 10:00–10:15 p.m.
required_facets: All listed breaks, exact start/end time and paid/unpaid if specified

question: What should an employee do if they cannot take their regular break because they are attending a meeting during break time?
expected_answer: An employee who cannot take the regular break because of a meeting may take the break at another schedule, provided they obtain approval from their immediate superior. The superior will inform the HR Department and General Manager. The employee must also eat in an inconspicuous area such as the pantry or stock room.
required_facets: Superior approval, HR/GM notification, inconspicuous eating location

question: What activities are considered violations of the break time policy during overtime?
expected_answer: During overtime, employees are expected to perform work outside the specified break periods. Activities unrelated to work during other times may violate the break time policy. Examples include eating, watching TV, reading newspapers or magazines, sleeping, playing games, listening to music, brushing teeth, or other activities that do not concern work.
required_facets: Nonwork examples and applicability during OT outside designated breaks

question: When should the main office door be used for visitors and clients?
expected_answer: The main office door shall be used for accepting visitors and clients from 7:30 AM to 7:00 PM. The Administration Department shall close it at 7:00 PM unless there are visitors from the client side.
required_facets: Visitor entrance window 7:30AM–7PM and client exception

question: If two employees are the last to leave the office after working overtime, who is responsible for locking the back door?
expected_answer: If two or more employees are the last to leave, the highest-ranking employee is responsible. If they are of the same level, the employee with the most years of service is in charge. If they have the same rank and tenure, all of them must sign the checklist.
required_facets: Highest rank, then longest service, then all sign for exact tie

question: What should an employee do if they work overtime on a weekend and need an office key?
expected_answer: An employee working overtime on weekends should borrow the duplicate key from their Department Manager. The employee must sign the key keeping logbook when borrowing and returning the office key. The employee is responsible for returning the key to the Department Manager on the following working day, subject to the policy's exceptions.
required_facets: Manager-issued duplicate key, logbook, next-working-day return

question: What happens if an employee loses a company office key or makes an unauthorized duplicate?
expected_answer: If an employee misplaces a company key, they are subject to disciplinary action and must shoulder the expenses for changing the company locks and duplicating new sets of keys. Unauthorized duplication of keys is considered a serious offense and is grounds for disciplinary action. Violations of the key keeping policy also have progressive penalties: 1st offense written warning, 2nd offense 1-day suspension, 3rd offense 3-day suspension, and 4th offense 5-day suspension.
required_facets: Lock replacement expenses; unauthorized copies serious offense; progressive penalties

question: How long can an employee's personal telephone call last, and what is required for a long-distance or overseas call?
expected_answer: Personal telephone calls should not exceed five (5) minutes. For long-distance or overseas calls, employees must log the date, time, place, and party to be called in the telephone logbook at the HR & Office Department. HROAD approval is required before placing the call.
required_facets: 5-minute personal limit; long-distance log fields and HROAD approval

question: Who is eligible for the Leveling Award System?
expected_answer: The Leveling Award System covers employees who have passed or topped the Japanese IT Standard Examination or Japanese Language Proficiency Test, employees who receive awards or citations from clients under the specified conditions, and employees who obtain grades of 96 and above in the in-house Nihonggo Classes Levels 1 to 4.
required_facets: Exams, client recognition conditions, in-house grade 96+

question: If a client gives an employee a certificate of award directly, can the employee qualify for the Leveling Award?
expected_answer: Yes. An employee may qualify when the client directly grants the employee a certificate of award. Client awards or citations are acknowledged and processed based on the conditions stated in the policy.
required_facets: Explicit Yes and client-issued certificate under policy conditions

question: What grade does an employee need to obtain in the in-house Nihonggo Classes to qualify for the Leveling Award?
expected_answer: An employee must obtain a grade of 96 and above in the in-house Nihonggo Classes. The qualifying classes are Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, and Level 4.
required_facets: Grade 96+, Levels 1–4

question: When is the Leveling Award given to an employee?
expected_answer: The award shall be given after the results have been announced or informed to the HR and Office Administration Department. HROA then notifies the Administration Manager and advises Finance to prepare the necessary amount for the award.
required_facets: Results announced → HROA → Admin Manager → Finance

question: When and where are Leveling Awards given to employees?
expected_answer: Awarding of employees shall be done during afternoon briefings. Employees with Level 1 classification will receive further acknowledgement through an announcement at the Christmas Party.
required_facets: Afternoon briefing; Level 1 Christmas Party acknowledgment

question: What should an employee do if their departure flight is delayed?
expected_answer: An employee on a business visa must inform their immediate superior at the Supervisory or Managerial Level if their departure flight from the Philippine International Airport or Japan International Airport is delayed. The immediate superior will inform the ZZZZ Administrative Manager, General Manager, and XXXX and coordinate necessary changes to pick-up arrangements and client notifications.
required_facets: Employee → immediate superior; superior → admin/GM/partner; pickups/clients

question: Who is responsible for handling the necessary arrangements when an employee's flight is delayed or cancelled?
expected_answer: The employee must inform their immediate superior. The immediate superior is responsible for informing the ZZZZ Administrative Manager, General Manager, and XXXX, and coordinating with the Administrative Manager and XXXX regarding changes to pick-up arrangements and informing clients.
required_facets: Responsible immediate superior, full recipient list, coordination

question: What should an employee do if the company's pick-up arrangement is no longer available because of a delayed flight?
expected_answer: The employee may request the airline officer to provide transportation to the hotel or apartment where the employee will be accommodated. Expenses caused by the delayed flight should appropriately be shouldered by the airline, and the employee is expected to assert this right.
required_facets: Unavailability of original transport, airline officer request, airline expenses

question: What should an employee do if a delayed flight requires an overnight stay because transportation is unavailable upon arrival?
expected_answer: The employee should request the airline officer to arrange hotel accommodation when an overnight stay is necessary because transportation is unavailable at the time of arrival. The hotel accommodation should be charged to the airline.
required_facets: Overnight stay when no transport; hotel arranged by airline and charged to airline

question: If a flight is delayed for one day or more because of airline negligence, who should pay for additional expenses such as food and laundry?
expected_answer: The employee's daily allowances remain the same based on the original or extended business trip schedule in Japan. If the flight is delayed for one day or more due to airline negligence, incurred expenses such as food and laundry services should be charged to the airline.
required_facets: Delay 1+ day because of airline negligence; allowances unchanged; food/laundry charged airline

question: What is the purpose of the Company's employee benefits program?
expected_answer: The Company's benefits program supports the professional development and personal growth of employees. It provides benefits to reward or compensate good performance and productivity, maintain industrial peace, address employee needs, provide protection from financial hardships, replace income when work stops due to sickness, disability, old age or death, attract and retain capable employees, and improve corporate efficiency.
required_facets: Reward, protection, industrial relations, employee development and retention

question: How many vacation leave days does a regular employee receive after completing one year of continuous service?
expected_answer: A regular employee who has completed at least one full year of continuous service from the date of hiring is granted fifteen (15) working days of annual vacation leave with pay. During the first year, the employee begins earning leave credits that can be used during the second year.
required_facets: One year regular employee, 15 working days with pay, accrual and usage

question: If two employees in the same department request vacation leave for the same period, who gets priority?
expected_answer: If there is a conflict in scheduling vacation leaves among employees in the same department, the employee with the greatest length of service will be given priority.
required_facets: Same department and overlapping VL; greatest tenure priority

question: Who is considered an immediate family member for purposes of bereavement leave?
expected_answer: Immediate family includes the legal spouse, legitimate and illegitimate children, parents including adoptive parents, grandparents, and brothers or sisters including half-brothers and half-sisters. For the death of a spouse's relatives, such as parents-in-law or brothers/sisters-in-law, the employee may apply for vacation leave instead of bereavement leave.
required_facets: Enumerated immediate family, relatives-in-law treated differently

question: What happens if an employee does not notify their immediate superior when taking bereavement leave?
expected_answer: An employee intending to take bereavement leave should seek permission from the immediate superior on the day of absence through telephone, email, telegram, or letter. If the superior is unavailable, the employee should notify HR. Failure to notify the appropriate person makes the absence Absence Without Leave (AWOL) and subjects the employee to disciplinary action under Level II Misconduct.
required_facets: Same-day contact immediate superior or HR fallback; AWOL and disciplinary consequence

question: Who is entitled to receive the full mid-year bonus?
expected_answer: Regular employees who have stayed in the Company for at least one year as of the May 31 bonus period cut-off are entitled to receive the mid-year bonus in full. Regular employees who have stayed less than one year receive a pro-rated bonus based on their length of stay.
required_facets: Regular status, ≥1 year as of May 31, pro-rata if shorter

question: When is the mid-year bonus paid, and when is the year-end bonus paid?
expected_answer: The mid-year bonus is paid to employees not later than June 30. The year-end bonus is paid not later than December 15.
required_facets: Midyear by June 30 and year-end by Dec 15

question: Who is entitled to the annual merit increase, and when does it take effect?
expected_answer: Employees who have stayed in the Company for at least one year are entitled to the annual merit increase. The increase is effective in July of every year. The percentage varies depending on Company profitability and management discretion and is subject to the approved budget.
required_facets: ≥1 year, July effective date, variable management/budget factors

question: Can an employee receive a 0% annual merit increase?
expected_answer: Yes. If an employee's performance appraisal shows a poor rating, management has the prerogative to give the employee a zero percent (0%) annual merit increase.
required_facets: Explicit Yes and poor appraisal/management prerogative

question: What health benefits does the Company provide to regular employees?
expected_answer: The Company provides all regular employees with Health Insurance, Optical Benefit, and a Physical Wellness Program.
required_facets: Health insurance, optical benefit, physical wellness

question: What is the purpose of the company's Training & Development policy?
expected_answer: The policy aims to enhance, cultivate, redirect, focus, and apply employees' collective skills, potential, and capabilities toward the goals of the organization. It recognizes employees as the company's most important resource and seeks to understand their strengths, weaknesses, skills, character, personality, talents, belief systems, and motivation.
required_facets: All policy objectives/skills and organizational alignment

question: When should an employee attend the Orientation Seminar?
expected_answer: All employees shall have an Orientation Seminar within a month of receiving their Notice Personnel Action of Regularization. The seminar is given by the Human Resources and Office Administration Department.
required_facets: Within 1 month after regularization NPA, HROA

question: What topics are discussed during the Orientation Seminar?
expected_answer: The Orientation Seminar covers company history and organization, personnel policies, terms of employment, personnel activities and benefit plans, company activities, compensation and salary administration, promotion or salary increase opportunities, and the employee's job and assigned department.
required_facets: All enumerated orientation agenda items

question: Who is required to undergo Basic Technical Training Courses, and how are trainees evaluated?
expected_answer: All engineering personnel are required to undergo Basic Technical Training Courses. The courses are organized by HROAD and Engineering Trainors. Trainors evaluate each trainee's learning level and skill through design reviews for each programming exercise or machine problem.
required_facets: All engineering personnel; HROAD/trainors; design-review assessment

question: Is the evaluation from Basic Technical Training the only basis for an employee's regularization?
expected_answer: No. The trainors' evaluation is used as a reference for regularization, but it is not the only basis. Character, work ethic, personality, ability to work, and ability to blend with the team, among others, are also considered.
required_facets: Explicit No; evaluation is reference, other listed factors

question: Who must attend the Personality Development and Professional Attitude Enhancement Seminar, and how long does it usually take?
expected_answer: All Design Engineer I and administration staff shall undergo the Personality Development and Professional Attitude Enhancement Seminar. The seminar usually takes one day, or 8 hours.
required_facets: Design Engineer I and admin staff, usually 8 hours

question: What training is required for Design Engineer II, and what are its objectives?
expected_answer: All Design Engineer II shall undergo a Leadership Training Seminar. Its objectives include understanding basic leadership principles and theories, developing and enhancing leadership potential and skills, and applying the concepts to themselves and their relationships with co-employees, peers, superiors, and subordinates.
required_facets: Design Engineer II; 3 leadership objectives

question: What training is required for Jr. Engineering Supervisors or Engineering Supervisors, and what topics does it cover?
expected_answer: Jr. Engineering Supervisors or Engineering Supervisors are required to attend Advanced Supervisory Training Seminars. The topics are Goal Setting & Achieving Organizational Effectiveness, Project Planning & Management, Quality Control, and Effective Presentation Skills.
required_facets: Junior/Engineering Supervisors; all four agenda topics

question: What training must all Managers undergo, and what subjects are included?
expected_answer: All Managers shall undergo a Management Training Seminar covering Manpower Planning and Development, Marketing Management, Production Management, and Accounting and Financial Management. Participants are also required to evaluate the training attended.
required_facets: All managers; four agenda subjects; training evaluation

question: How are In-House Technical Trainings organized and approved?
expected_answer: Engineering Managers and Officers of each department organize in-house technical training programs, independently or with HROAD or other engineering departments. The officer-in-charge must prepare a course syllabus and schedule. These are checked by the respective Managers and approved by the Engineering Director or Vice President. Participants evaluate the technical training, and the trainer reports the result to the respective Manager, ED, and Vice President.
required_facets: Organizers, syllabus+schedule, Manager review, ED/VP approval, evaluations and reporting
